findings.evidence: .github/workflows/update.yml:3-5 "Keeps the mathlib pin moving using the leanprover-community/downstream-reports ... open/update a single 'bump to last-known-good' PR"; docs/dependency-bumps.md:109-110 "Until the bump-guard step lands, `check-bump.sh` still accepts only a mathlib move on master ... which no three-dependency bump satisfies."
findings.fix: Say what holds today — the Mathlib pin can only move to a commit all three libraries build against, so it waits for the slowest — and drop the claim that a bump selects a new set of commits for each library, or add the paragraph with the PR that wires the resolver into `update.yml`.
findings.issue: "Dependency bumps therefore move to the newest set of commits that fit together, not to the newest commit of each library" states on the public site a policy nothing implements: `update.yml` still bumps mathlib alone from downstream-reports, the resolver is not called by anything (PR description: "nothing calls it yet"), and the guard rejects any bump that moves Physlib/TauCeti at all.

findings.evidence: docs/dependency-bumps.md:105 "`update.yml` runs the resolver ..., records failed sets | planned" and :107 "EpsilonEridaniWorker's `bump` stage hands back a PR whose build fails inside a dependency | planned".
findings.fix: Put it in the future ("will be passed back ... once the `bump` stage lands") or state that only the `--exclude` flag exists today, so the section does not contradict the Status table 40 lines below.
findings.issue: "a set whose build fails inside a dependency ... is passed back with `--exclude` so the next feasible set is tried" is present tense, but the same file's Status table lists both the worker `bump` stage that would hand the set back and the `update.yml` job that would record it as planned. A reader of the section alone concludes the loop runs.

findings.evidence: scripts/lean_versions.py:28-29 `return parse_release(name) or (math.inf,) * 4`; :47-48 `return (toolchain or "?").strip().removeprefix(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)` — every other function in the file is documented.
findings.fix: One line each: `release_key` — "sort key; a name that is not a release sorts after every release"; `show_toolchain` — "the version for display, `?` when there is no pin".
findings.issue: In a new module whose stated job is the one parse/order rule for every script, `release_key` (line 28) and `show_toolchain` (line 47) carry no docstring, and their fallbacks are invisible: an unparseable name gets `(inf,)*4`, i.e. sorts as newer than every real release, and `show_toolchain(None)` yields the literal `"?"`.

summary: The resolver's module docstring and the dependency-bumps doc are accurate about the algorithm, but two places describe not-yet-wired behaviour in the present tense — including on the public About page — and the new shared `lean_versions.py` leaves two helpers with non-obvious fallbacks undocumented.
